transcript.text: Bosch SMS2HVI67G showing E:25 and won't drain. A wine glass smashed in it last night if that's relevant?

Yes, very relevant. It's probably the cause. E:25 on a Bosch dishwasher means it can't pump the water out: the drain is blocked or the pump is jammed. Small shards of glass are one of the classic things that get past the filter and lodge in the drain pump, stopping the little impeller from turning. Most likely causes, in order:
1. Glass jammed in the drain pump under the small pump cover in the sump.
2. Glass and food debris blocking the filter or sump.
3. Less likely: a kinked drain hose or blocked sink waste. It could be coincidence, but the timing points to the glass. Switch the dishwasher off and unplug it first. Wear thick gloves throughout, because there will be sharp fragments. Have towels ready. 1. Take out the lower basket and check the bottom of the tub for loose glass. Then twist and lift out the filter. Rinse it carefully, wearing gloves, and pick out any glass. A gritty or blocked filter would explain it.
2. Bail out any standing water with a cup and sponge. In the sump there's a small (often white) pump cover. Lift its clip, tilt it out and look underneath with a torch. Glass here is very likely. Remove any pieces, ideally with tongs or long-nose pliers rather than fingers. Then turn the impeller gently with a gloved finger. If it turns freely with nothing caught, that's good. If it's chipped or broken, the pump will need replacing.
3. Refit the cover and filter. Check the grey drain hose behind the plinth and under the sink isn't kinked, and that the sink drains normally.
4. Plug back in and run a short rinse or drain programme, listening near the bottom of the machine. If the water pumps away, you're sorted. If it still shows E:25 with everything clear, the drain pump itself may have been damaged. A pump that hums but doesn't move water usually still has a jam. One that's completely silent points more to the pump or its connection. Let me know what you find under that pump cover.

Did all that with gloves on. Big bits of glass in the filter, and under the pump cover there was a sliver wedged against the impeller. I got it out with tongs and the impeller now turns freely. Cover clicked back in, drain hose is fine, and a drain/rinse now pumps out with no E:25.

That's a textbook fix. The sliver against the impeller was what triggered E:25. 1. Run a normal programme next and check it completes without the code. Tiny fragments sometimes work loose on the first wash, so give the filter one more rinse afterwards (with gloves on) to catch anything that's come out.
2. Check the lower spray arm holes and the basket runners for any small shards. Those are the other places glass tends to hide.
3. From now on, give the filter a quick twist-out and rinse every week or two. It keeps debris from building up and reaching the pump in the first place. If E:25 ever comes back, or you hear a grinding or crunching noise during draining, there's probably another fragment in the sump. Repeat the same check under the pump cover. Anything else I can help with?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]

Drain filter / sump blocked with glass and debris (medium)
Kinked or blocked drain hose / sink waste (low)

plan: They asked: "Is the wine glass that smashed in it last night relevant?" - answer that first.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Bosch; model SMS2HVI67G; code E:25.
The fault they reported is: "won't drain". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

Explain what the error code means using ERROR CODES. If ERROR CODES does not resolve it, say plainly that you cannot confirm what it means on their model (it may not be an error code at all, for example part of the model name), never guess a meaning, and work from the symptoms.
